```{r load-data, include=FALSE}
# Load your data here
# Load data set
student_math <- read_rds("data/student_math.rds")

# Remove unnecessary columns and missing mathematics scores
student_math_pro <- student_math |>
  select(-general_family_support) |>
  filter(
    if_all(
      starts_with("math_score_pv"),
      ~ !is.na(.)
    )
  )

# Select variables for the investigation
student_processed <- student_math_pro |>
  select(
    student_id,
    country_code,
    student_age,
    student_gender,
    family_socioeconomic_status,
    family_support,
    home_possessions_index,
    home_ict_resources,
    highest_parental_education,
    parental_education_years,
    highest_parental_occupational_status,
    starts_with("math_score_pv")
  )

# Calculate mean mathematics score
student_processed <- student_processed |>
  mutate(
    math_score = rowMeans(
      across(starts_with("math_score_pv"))
    )
  ) |>
  select(-starts_with("math_score_pv"))

```

## Research question

**How are parental education, parental occupational status, and home ICT resources associated with students’ mathematics performance in PISA 2025?**

--

**Why it matters**

- Students' home environments may play an important role in their educational outcomes. Differences in parental education, occupational status, and access to ICT resources may be associated with students' opportunities to learn and their mathematics performance. Investigating these relationships can help us better understand how family background relates to educational achievement.

---

class: inverse, center, middle

# Data

---

# Data

**Dataset overview:**
- Student-level data from the PISA 2025 Student Questionnaire (OECD)
- 755,721 students · 90 countries and economies · 24 variables
- Used to examine the link between family background and mathematics achievement
- Citation: OECD (n.d.) *PISA 2025 Student Questionnaire*. Retrieved [date]

---

**Original data:**
- 755,721 students from 90 countries/regions
- 24 variables
- Included student information, family background, home resources and mathematics scores.

**Data cleaning:**
- **Starting point:** the data file and the student questionnaire; the questionnaire was set aside and everything is based on the 755,721 student rows in `student_math`
- **Check:** `summary()` in R to identify missing values
- **Exclude:** Uzbekistan (all of its records) and Belgium (one record)
- **Filter missing values:** 8,653 missing per score variable → 747,068 records remain
- **Select:** maths scores, parental education, parental occupational status, home ICT resources
- **Combine:** `rowMeans()` average of the ten scores → `math_score`; the ten original columns removed
- **Remaining missing values:** not removed at this stage, but excluded as each visualisation or analysis needs them

*Result: `student_math` 755,721 × 24 → `student_math_pro` 747,068 × 23 (after dropping `general_family_support`) → `student_processed` 747,068 × 12 (ten plausible values became one `math_score`)*

# Visualization

---

# Overall mathematics performance
```{r Visualising-overall, echo=FALSE}
# Calculate the 2.5th and 97.5th percentiles
ci <- quantile(
  student_processed$math_score,
  probs = c(0.025, 0.975)
)

ggplot(student_processed, aes(x = math_score)) +
  geom_histogram(
    bins = 50,
    fill = "steelblue",
    color = "white"
  ) +
  geom_vline(
    xintercept = ci,
    color = "#D98282",
    linetype = "dashed",
    linewidth = 1
  ) +
  annotate(
    "text",
    x = ci[1],
    y = Inf,
    label = paste0("2.5%: ", round(ci[1], 2)),
    color = "#D98282",
    vjust = 1.5,
    size = 3.5
  ) +
  annotate(
    "text",
    x = ci[2],
    y = Inf,
    label = paste0("97.5%: ", round(ci[2], 2)),
    color = "#D98282",
    vjust = 1.5,
    size = 3.5
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Distribution of Mathematics Scores",
    subtitle = "Central 95% of Mathematics Scores | PISA 2025",
    x = "Mathematics Score",
    y = "Number of Students"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()
```

---

```{r parental-education, echo=FALSE}
#the relationship between parental education years and mathematics score
# Prepare data
education_data <- student_processed %>%
  drop_na(parental_education_years,
    math_score) %>%
  mutate(
    parental_education = factor(
      as.numeric(parental_education_years)
    )
  )


# Violin plot
ggplot(
    education_data,
    aes(
        x = parental_education,
        y = math_score
    )
) +
    geom_violin(
        trim = TRUE,
        fill = "#DCD6F7",
        colour = "#7566A8",
        alpha = 0.8
    ) +
    geom_boxplot(
        width = 0.12,
        outlier.shape = NA,
        fill = "white",
        colour = "#493A70",
        linewidth = 0.5
    ) +
    labs(
        title = "Parental Education and Mathematics Performance",
        subtitle = "PISA 2025 Student Data",
        x = "Highest Education of Parents in Years",
        y = "Mathematics Score"
    ) +
    coord_flip() +
    theme_minimal()
```

```{r, echo=FALSE}
#the relationship between ICT and mathematics score
clean_data <- student_processed |>
     filter(
```

class: inverse, center, middle

# Findings and related discussion

---

```{r, echo=FALSE}
#correlation between conditions and math performance
correlation_data <- student_processed |>
    select(
        math_score,
        highest_parental_occupational_status,
        parental_education_years,
        home_ict_resources
    )

correlation_values <- correlation_data |>
    summarise(
        across(
            -math_score,
            ~ cor(.x, math_score, use = "complete.obs")
        )
    ) |>
    pivot_longer(
        everything(),
        names_to = "Variable",
        values_to = "Correlation"
    )
ggplot(
    correlation_values,
    aes(
        x = "Mathematics Score",
        y = Variable,
        fill = Correlation
    )
) +
    geom_tile(
        colour = "black",
        linewidth = 0.8
    ) +
    geom_text(
        aes(label = round(Correlation, 2)),
        size = 4
    ) +
    scale_fill_gradient2(
        low = "#2878B5",
        mid = "white",
        high = "#D65F73",
        midpoint = 0,
        limits = c(-1, 1),
        name = "Correlation"
    ) +
    labs(
        title = "Correlation with Mathematics Performance",
        subtitle = "PISA 2025 Student Data",
        x = NULL,
        y = NULL
    ) +
    theme_minimal()+
scale_y_discrete(labels = c(
    "highest_parental_occupational_status" = "Parental occupation",
    "parental_education_years" = "Highest education of parents in years",
    "home_ict_resources" = "Home ICT resources"
))

```

---

```{r, echo=FALSE}
# linear regression

model <- linear_reg() |>
  set_engine("lm") |>
  fit(
    math_score ~ highest_parental_occupational_status +
    parental_education_years +
    home_ict_resources,
  data = student_processed
)
summary(model$fit)
```

---

```{r, echo=FALSE}  
# linear regression with country factor
model2 <- linear_reg() |>
  set_engine("lm") |>
  fit(
    math_score ~ highest_parental_occupational_status +
    parental_education_years +
    home_ict_resources +
    factor(country_code),
  data = student_processed
)
summary(model2$fit)

```

---

# Math Expressions

The estimated regression model is:

$$\widehat{MathScore}_i =
  {`r model2$fit$coefficients[["(Intercept)"]] %>% sprintf(fmt='%.2f')`} +
  {`r model2$fit$coefficients[["highest_parental_occupational_status"]] %>% sprintf(fmt='%.2f')`} \times Occupation_i +
  {`r model2$fit$coefficients[["parental_education_years"]] %>% sprintf(fmt='%.2f')`} \times Education_i +
  {`r model2$fit$coefficients[["home_ict_resources"]] %>% sprintf(fmt='%.2f')`} \times ICT_i +
  \alpha_{Country(i)}$$

# Math Expressions

The estimated regression model is:

$$\widehat{MathScore}_i =
  {`r model2$fit$coefficients[["(Intercept)"]] %>% sprintf(fmt='%.2f')`} +
  {`r model2$fit$coefficients[["highest_parental_occupational_status"]] %>% sprintf(fmt='%.2f')`} \times Occupation_i +
  {`r model2$fit$coefficients[["parental_education_years"]] %>% sprintf(fmt='%.2f')`} \times Education_i +
  {`r model2$fit$coefficients[["home_ict_resources"]] %>% sprintf(fmt='%.2f')`} \times ICT_i +
  \alpha_{Country(i)}$$


Limitations:

1. The source code of a LaTeX math expression must be in one line, unless it is inside a pair of double dollar signs, in which case the starting `$$` must appear in the very beginning of a line, followed immediately by a non-space character, and the ending `$$` must be at the end of a line, led by a non-space character;

1. There should not be spaces after the opening `$` or before the closing `$`.

1. Math does not work on the title slide (see [#61](https://github.com/yihui/xaringan/issues/61) for a workaround).
